v0.1.0-rc.12.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.12
v0.1.0-rc.12.intro: A release candidate after v0.1.0-rc.11 that tightens Agent local writes, admin login lockout, configuration push, and runtime failure handling. Read-only status on the loopback admin page stays anonymous, and change endpoints require a local token. The admin endpoint stays plain HTTP by design.

sections.title: Highlights
items: The Agent loopback page still has no password. Read-only status stays anonymous. Changes to /api/v2/admin/* must carry the X-RelayLink-Local-Token request header. The token is stored beside agent.json in local-management.token: Unix mode 0600, and a Windows DACL limited to the current identity, SYSTEM, and Administrators. Importing useTls=false must also submit confirmInsecureTransport=CONNECT_WITHOUT_TLS. Successful creates, updates, deletes, and enable or disable writes go to the Agent file log, recording the configuration-item identifier, host, port, useTls, and the client identifier, without secrets or tokens. Enable or disable records the result already persisted while the change lock was held.

Admin login lockout now counts by the direct connection address and username. The same pair locks after five failures. The same address also has a combined limit of 20. A full state table returns 503 with Retry-After. Unexpired history is still not evicted. Forwarded headers are not read.

After the client file and listeners have already been updated, a configuration push that fails before any frame bytes are written returns 200 or 201 with pushedToAgent=false, and the control session stays. A failure after a frame write or flush has started closes that session, because the byte stream may already be out of sync. Saved files are not rolled back.

PeerOpen and PeerOpenGranted carry setupTimeoutMilliseconds, the sum of openTimeoutSeconds and the target channel's targetConnectTimeoutSeconds. v3 and v4 frames keep the field. The current Agent uses that value when the frame version is 3 or 4, including budgets longer than 20 seconds. Agents released earlier ignore the unknown JSON and still use the built-in 20-second cap.
The Agent ApplyConfiguration validates every outbound mapping before it stops or creates listeners.
Heartbeat time and RTT are published from the same immutable snapshot. A failed TryRegister abandons the session that has not yet been used.

The proxy accept loop retries a recoverable socket error at most three times. Once those retries are exhausted it logs and degrades /health/ready. Retrying a single recoverable error does not clear readiness. A failed listener is replaced the next time configuration is applied successfully, and /health/ready returns to 200.
Each session keeps a two-minute deduplication window for RequestId before the quota check. An unexpected exception in the relay RunAsync is logged and cleanup is completed.
A newly created mapping uses the LoadedConfiguration just read from disk.
A configuration access failure exits with code 2. UnauthorizedAccessException, SecurityException, and a failure to access the client directory are converted to ConfigurationException.
The overview, dashboards, channel list, and mapping status share the same channel-availability decision, including UDP on v3 clients.

On initial registration and on configuration updates, the Agent requires the snapshot ClientId to match the configuration item's ClientId, otherwise it throws AgentPermanentException. A correct configuration hash alone does not prove that the snapshot belongs to that item.

Before writing any bytes, FrameWriter rejects invalid DATA and FIN using the reader-side length rules. The UDP listener holds the session before calling the handler. A synchronous or asynchronous handler failure only cleans up that session and logs it, and does not stop the listener. A full UDP queue still drops the newest datagram. Each drop increments udpDroppedTotal on the channel snapshot and the dashboard snapshot. The Agent logs the cumulative value for that configuration item at most once every 30 seconds.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 remains v5, and JSON schemaVersion remains 1. Server continues to accept v3, v4, and v5.
The admin UI remains plain HTTP on loopback by design. Some frame deadlines remain a single overall time limit. Anonymous read-only admin status stays as designed.

When calling an Agent change endpoint, read the token from local-management.token and set X-RelayLink-Local-Token. When importing useTls=false, also submit confirmInsecureTransport=CONNECT_WITHOUT_TLS.
Agents that predate setupTimeoutMilliseconds ignore the field, and peer setup remains limited to 20 seconds. The current Agent also uses the server-supplied budget for v3 and v4 frames.

When the configuration is already on disk and the push fails before any frame bytes are written, the save succeeds with pushedToAgent=false and the files are not rolled back. A failure halfway through a write closes the control session.
When the snapshot ClientId does not match the configuration item, the Agent refuses registration and later configuration updates.

Ordinary TCP, UDP, and HTTP forwarding remains that of v0.1.0-rc.11. This candidate also rejects invalid DATA and FIN before writing, isolates a failed UDP session handler, and counts queue drops in udpDroppedTotal.

sections.title: Verification and limitations

#9 moves test-fixture temporary directories off the shared ACL. #12 adds a DeepSeek Claude Code review workflow on a private runner. Both affect only tests and CI.
This candidate has no new TestClient-01 Docker smoke record. Windows installers are unsigned, and macOS archives are unsigned and not notarized, the same as v0.1.0-rc.11.

v0.1.0-rc.11.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.11
v0.1.0-rc.11.intro: A release candidate after v0.1.0-rc.10 that tightens the management plane, runtime connection limits, and secret-file permissions. The admin endpoint stays plain HTTP and the examples and Docker setup listen on loopback by default. Client connection limits apply immediately, and TCP connections that are silent in both directions close after the server idle timeout.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Example configs and Docker bind dashboard.listenAddress to 127.0.0.1. A non-loopback admin listener writes a SECURITY error to the log and stderr, and the process still starts. The recommended path is still an Agent on the server and an end-to-end encrypted peer channel to the admin UI on 127.0.0.1. This candidate does not add mandatory admin HTTPS.

Passwords longer than 1024 UTF-8 bytes are rejected before PBKDF2. A wrong username still runs PBKDF2. Five failures from the same source lock that source, with backoff from 1 second up to 15 minutes. After a lock expires, one in-flight retry is allowed and failures keep accumulating. The failure cache holds at most 10,000 sources, keeps unexpired history when it prunes, and refuses new sources when it is full of unexpired state.
An existing login session is replaced only after the login-success audit event is stored. If that write fails, login returns 503 and the previous session stays valid.

Before the secret has been checked, ClientNotFound, ClientDisabled, and InvalidSecret are sent to the peer as AuthenticationFailed. The detailed reasons stay in the audit log and server logs. Failures after the secret check stay specific.
Every management response sets Content-Security-Policy (including frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY. /api stays Cache-Control: no-store.

Client maxConnections and maxPendingConnections take effect immediately. Lowering a limit blocks new slots. Connections that already hold a permit keep it until they finish, and releasing one does not open a slot above the new maximum. Saving a client limit pushes a configuration snapshot to a ready Agent.

Channel and client updates write the JSON first, then switch listeners and the in-memory configuration. If binding fails, the previous file is written back and existing connections stay. A client directory that cannot accept the temp file fails before any listener changes. Deleting a client removes the file first and restores it if the listener update fails.

limits.tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds cancels an established ordinary TCP proxy or authorized peer relay when both directions have been silent for that long, then releases the connection slot. Omitting the field uses 900 seconds; 0 disables idle close. Accepted TCP sockets enable keepalive, and the admin overview shows the active value. Cancellation while waiting for an unauthenticated handshake slot, or a full slot, disposes the accepted socket on the control and data acceptors. RegisterAccepted carries halfCloseDrainTimeoutSeconds and tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds. Current Agents use those values for ordinary TCP relays and for encrypted or plaintext peer copies, including half-close drain. Older peers ignore the new fields. The values follow server.json and are picked up on the next registration.

Client JSON, rewritten server.json, and the SQLite audit and traffic files are readable only by the service account: Unix mode 0600, database directories created for them 0700, and a Windows DACL for the current process identity with inheritance removed. A group- or world-readable secret, private key, client directory, or database is reported as SECURITY in the log and on stderr. Other-writable shared database directories, the process temp directory, /tmp, a filesystem root, and any existing other-writable directory are refused, and the process asks for a RelayLink-only directory. A dedicated database directory is tightened so later WAL and SHM files are not world-readable; a shared parent is not rewritten. The systemd unit sets UMask=0077. Linux deployment docs match the Agent docs: /etc/relaylink and clients are 0700, and secret files are 0600.
Third-party GitHub Actions in CI, release, and Pages are pinned to commit SHAs, with the version tag kept in a comment.

The root README no longer describes the HTTP design as unimplemented. The HTTP design stays Draft and now says the v5 path is on main, while the evaluation and unmeasured capacity sections remain draft. Linux and Windows deployment notes no longer require upgrading Server and Agent together. They follow the v3 TCP / v4 UDP / v5 HTTP matrix and point at the UDP and HTTP operations guides.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 remains v5, and JSON schemaVersion remains 1. Server continues to accept v3, v4, and v5.
The admin UI remains plain HTTP on loopback by design.

Before upgrading, confirm that secret paths and database directories meet the new permission checks. Windows Docker Desktop bind mounts may need an explicit chmod 0700 or 0600 inside the Linux VM. Omitting tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds now defaults to 900 seconds; set 0 to keep the previous behavior of no application idle timeout.
Otherwise, ordinary TCP/UDP and HTTP proxy behavior is unchanged from v0.1.0-rc.10.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: The merged changes #3 (890a282), #4 (d9e03b8), and #2 (e5834f5) passed CI on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon).

Live Docker smoke on TestClient-01 (Windows, Docker Desktop 29.5.3) at e5834f5: /health/ready and /health/live returned 200; the admin UI returned 200 with CSP, X-Frame-Options, and nosniff; the admin listener inside the container was 127.0.0.1:18080. Docker Desktop network_mode: host is the Linux VM host, not Windows loopback; that was checked with a host-network sidecar.

Known Windows Desktop friction: the admin password is entered interactively on the first compose start, and bind-mount modes need chmod inside the VM. This note does not include multipass or remote test-server verification.
Windows installers are unsigned, and macOS archives are unsigned and not notarized, the same as v0.1.0-rc.10.

v0.1.0-rc.10.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.10
v0.1.0-rc.10.intro: A release candidate that adds HTTP/HTTPS application proxying on the target Agent. Public listeners and encrypted peer access are both checked and forwarded to a fixed web upstream, with tighter WebSocket origin checks, idle timeouts, and client-address header handling.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Adds an HTTP application protocol. The target Agent forwards authorized HTTP/1.1 requests through a Kestrel virtual ingress and YARP, including HTTP/HTTPS, WebSocket, SSE, and streaming bodies. The business ingress does not open an extra operating-system listener, and neither Server nor the caller Agent parses HTTP.

A public channel is accepted by Server and delivered to the target Agent over the data tunnel. Authorized peer access still uses the caller loopback and inner TLS between Agents. Both paths validate and rewrite Host and Origin using the channel policy.
PEM certificates for HTTPS ingress keep their intermediate chain and pass it to Kestrel ServerCertificateChain, without relying on system trust or AIA downloads.

WebSocket Upgrade tokens are recognized individually when separated by commas. Public and peer channels both require a non-empty Origin allowlist. An empty list rejects WebSocket handshakes, including those with a missing Origin or the same origin.

Public WebSocket idle timeout now defaults to 300 seconds and can no longer be set to 0. Peer channels may still set 0 explicitly to disable idle close. A maxWebSocketConnections value of 0 uses the channel connection limit.

Forwarded, X-Forwarded-*, X-Real-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Client-IP, and CF-Connecting-IP are always removed, then forwarding headers are rebuilt from the authenticated ingress. stripRequestHeaders only adds exact header names; an empty list or a null entry cannot re-enable the built-in set. Revoking, disabling, or changing a channel disposes and removes its HTTP host.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 is now v5. Server accepts v3/v4/v5 and can be upgraded first. Existing v3 Agents keep ordinary and authorized peer TCP, and v4 Agents keep TCP/UDP. HTTP is sent only to v5, and the target Agent must be v5. HTTP peer access also requires a v5 caller with endToEndEncryptionEnabled=true. Versions 1/2, unknown versions, and version changes within a connection are rejected. New Agents do not automatically fall back when connecting to an old Server.

JSON schemaVersion is unchanged. Channels without applicationProtocol stay raw. HTTP channels must use TCP. HTTP policy and certificates take effect after the related Agent restarts; there is no hot reload.

Breaking configuration changes: publicAllowedOrigins and peerAllowedOrigins must both be non-empty Origin allowlists. An empty list can no longer skip origin checks. Public webSocketActivityTimeoutSeconds can no longer be 0; omitting it defaults to 300 seconds. Peer channels may still set 0 explicitly. Before upgrading, fill in the allowlists and check the public idle timeout using the HTTP operations guide.

Back up configuration, identity, Server SQLite data, and certificates before upgrading. Public HTTP has no browser TLS and is only for protected networks or tests that explicitly accept plaintext. Ordinary TCP/UDP behavior remains that of v0.1.0-rc.9.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: HTTP proxying and these security fixes passed 137 local unit tests and 81 integration tests with peer TLS enabled. Coverage includes origin rejection, HTTP status lines assembled from partial reads, WebSocket idle and concurrency limits, client-address header stripping, host disposal, and HTTPS intermediate chains. This note does not treat an unreplayed v3/v4 binary matrix or unrun cross-platform CI as completed acceptance.

Real-browser login, cookies, CSRF, and long-running capacity checks remain outstanding. The HTTP requirement stays Accepted and the design stays Draft. HTTP/2, HTTP/3, gRPC, and CONNECT forward proxying are unsupported, and response bodies are not rewritten.
Windows installers are unsigned; macOS packages are unsigned and not notarized. Requirements, design, and ADR review status remain as marked in their respective documents.

v0.1.0-rc.9.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.9
v0.1.0-rc.9.intro: A release candidate adding UDP forwarding and a multipage product website. This rebuilt release includes v3 client compatibility; earlier assets under the same version do not. Download again and verify the latest SHA256SUMS.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Ordinary and authorized peer channels support unicast UDP, isolate sessions by source address and port, and preserve empty datagrams and payloads up to 65507 bytes.
UDP travels through the existing TCP data tunnel with a separate target socket per source. Bounded queues, connection quotas, and idle cleanup retain authentication, security groups, and auditing.

The management UI supports TCP/UDP selection and UDP idle timeout configuration. Configuration snapshots, both dashboards, and read APIs show the protocol; online protocol changes recreate the related listeners.
UDP socket send buffers are at least 128 KiB, fixing large datagram failures caused by macOS defaults.
The product website now has separate home, guide, documentation, and release list/detail pages, with Chinese and English UDP usage, design, and upgrade guidance.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: NTP1 is now v4. Server accepts v3/v4, so it can be upgraded first while v3 Agents retain ordinary and authorized peer TCP forwarding. Responses and configuration hashes follow each session version, including mixed old/new peers. Consecutive configuration updates are acknowledged individually, fixing a race that overwrote pending versions and disconnected clients. UDP is sent only to v4 clients and requires all participating Agents to support v4. Versions 1/2, unknown versions, and version changes within a connection are rejected. New Agents do not automatically fall back when connecting to an old Server.
JSON schemaVersion is unchanged. Existing channels without transportProtocol default to TCP. UDP idle timeout defaults to 60 seconds and accepts 1–3600 seconds.

Update installed Windows Agents while preserving configuration and identity. Back up configuration, identity, Server SQLite data, and certificates before upgrading; see the UDP operations guide for details.
Ordinary UDP tunnels retain the plaintext data endpoint; authorized peer traffic uses inner TLS by default. Configure security groups, firewalls, and link protection for your deployment.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: CI for UDP and the macOS fix passed website, Linux, Windows, macOS Intel, and Apple Silicon checks. This compatibility fix passed 101 local unit tests and 59 full integration tests, including 9 tests using unmodified rc.8 Agents for ordinary TCP, old-client UDP rejection, mixed old/new peers with TLS or plaintext, and half-close. Peer TLS and the legacy binary matrix were enabled with no skips; the rebuilt tag runs full regular CI again.
UDP tests cover 0/1/32769/65507-byte datagrams, source isolation, idle cleanup, security groups, and online UDP/TCP changes, alongside existing TCP regression tests.

Real UDP applications across public networks, 24-hour capacity checks, and target-environment installation validation remain outstanding. Broadcast, multicast, and IP networking are unsupported. UDP over TCP can cause head-of-line blocking and has no real-time latency guarantee.
Windows installers are unsigned; macOS packages are unsigned and not notarized. Requirements, design, and ADR review status remain as marked in their respective documents.

v0.1.0-rc.8.intro: A release candidate focused on file logging, connection rejection diagnostics, and Windows Agent configuration saving.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Server and Agent share structured JSONL file logging through Serilog. Agent logging no longer depends on a Windows Event Log source.
Information and Warning logs are retained for 14 days. All files roll daily or at 10 MiB; separate Error and Critical logs are never automatically deleted by age or file count.

Control rejection messages include reasons such as missing or disabled clients, invalid secrets, identity mismatch, and duplicate sessions. Agent logs include the rejection code, reason, and connection stage without secrets, private keys, or application payloads.
Server supports --log-directory. Docker and systemd deployments use /var/lib/relaylink/logs, with Docker logs persisted in the existing data volume.
Windows installation and updates repair LocalService write permissions on agent.json, fixing Unable to save Agent configuration during local JSON imports.
Adds logging requirements, technical design, deployment guidance, and bilingual website explanations.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Use the preserve-state update path for installed Windows Agents. The installer also repairs old configuration permissions. Agent logs are stored in C:\ProgramData\RelayLink\Agent\logs.
The control protocol remains v3 with an optional rejection reason field. Upgrade both Server and Agent for complete reasons; older versions remain compatible but may only show a generic error code.

Connection rejection is a Warning and follows the 14-day retention policy. Permanent retention applies to Error and Critical only. Business diagnostic traces and SQLite audit retain their existing policies.

Read routine runtime events from log files. Container stderr and systemd journal mainly cover startup and logging failures. Operators should monitor capacity and archive permanently retained error files.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: The local .NET solution build, 82 unit tests, and 30 integration tests passed. One peer TLS test was skipped by local defaults; the release pipeline enables it.

Coverage includes log rolling and retention, rejection reasons, duplicate sessions, configuration acknowledgement rejection, and sensitive-field checks. Server bootstrap errors and configuration-check mode were also checked locally.

Docker Compose configuration parsing passed. A new container image run and target-environment installation validation remain outstanding. Windows installers are unsigned; macOS packages are unsigned and not notarized.

v0.1.0-rc.7.intro: A release candidate focused on multi-server Agent connections, local management, and cross-platform delivery.

sections.title: Highlights
items: One Agent can connect to multiple servers with separate client secrets, TLS trust, and runtime state. Channels and access mappings remain managed by their respective servers.

The Agent local dashboard is now a standalone React frontend. Profiles can be added or modified only by importing a single-server JSON file, and can be disabled, re-enabled, or deleted. Disabling disconnects the profile and stops retries while preserving its configuration and identity across restarts.
A standalone pre-start migrator converts legacy single-server configuration and identity state to the servers[] format. Windows, Linux, and macOS startup paths run the migrator before the Agent.
Windows Agent now has both self-contained and framework-dependent program archives and installers. Program files stay in the Agent install root; configuration and state stay in ProgramData.
Fixes the .NET 10 Docker build image selection and UTF-8 BOM handling during Windows configuration migration.
The bilingual product site now explains multi-server Agent connections, JSON import, and profile disabling. The tag triggers both website deployment and software package release.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Use the preserve-state update path for an installed Agent. First install and reconfiguration accept only the new JSON format. Reconfiguration resets managed local state and is unsuitable when retaining the end-to-end identity.
Legacy configuration must be migrated before the new Agent starts. A failed conversion prevents startup while retaining the original configuration and identity state for investigation and retry.
The proxy wire protocol is unchanged. The Agent dashboard binds only to 127.0.0.1; writes require a local session and CSRF token, and read responses do not expose registration secrets.

sections.title: Highlights

Clients and channels support one or more manually managed tags, with tag filtering in admin lists.
The Agent management endpoint adds a read-only loopback HTTP API for local software to inspect channels and Agent-to-Agent access endpoints.
Agent-to-Agent channels add an end-to-end encryption switch that is enabled by default. When explicitly disabled, traffic is copied directly over the authenticated peer connection.
The peer protocol moves to version 3 and binds the encryption mode into handshake authentication to prevent mismatched configurations.

sections.title: Security and compatibility
items: Agent-to-Server control and raw data links continue to use TLS. The new option affects only peer application traffic on Agent-to-Agent channels.
Unencrypted peer mode retains mutual identity checks, channel authorization, session binding, resource limits, and connection revocation after configuration changes.
Server and all Agents participating in peer access must be upgraded together because older Agents cannot establish version 3 peer sessions.
The local read-only API binds only to `127.0.0.1` and exposes no configuration writes.

sections.title: Verification
items: 40 .NET unit tests and 29 integration tests passed, including peer TLS coverage.
8 admin frontend tests, the production build, and formatting checks passed.
Coverage includes encrypted-default compatibility, plaintext copying, handshake-mode validation, revocation after mode changes, and local API boundaries.

items: Upgrade the Server and all Agents together to avoid peer protocol version mismatches.
New peer-only channels enable end-to-end encryption by default. Disable it only after explicitly accepting plaintext application traffic on the relay path.

v0.1.0-rc.2.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.2
v0.1.0-rc.2.intro: This release restructures the tunnel, changes how Agent trust material is delivered, and adds end-to-end acceptance coverage using real database protocols.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Fully separates control and data channels. Application data connections are accepted only after the control channel authenticates.
After binding, standard data channels use simple bidirectional TCP stream copying without parsing or modifying the application protocol.
Completes Agent-to-Agent configuration, Agent identity verification, channel updates, and local endpoint rotation.
Embeds the trusted CA in downloaded Agent configuration instead of requiring a CA file path on the target machine.
Improves management forms and guidance for clients, channels, and Agent-to-Agent access endpoints.
Adds a desktop shortcut for the local read-only status page after Windows Agent installation.
Adds SQL Server and PostgreSQL acceptance scripts covering common queries, joins, and transaction rollback through both standard and encrypted peer paths.

sections.title: Upgrade notes
items: Control and data protocols changed. Upgrade the Server and Agents together and do not mix rc.1 and rc.2 components.
Download a fresh Agent configuration from the admin UI to avoid retaining obsolete trust settings.
Standard proxy data channels do not add encryption. Use application TLS or a protected network path for sensitive traffic.

v0.1.0-rc.13.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.13
v0.1.0-rc.13.intro: This release candidate after v0.1.0-rc.12 introduces auditable inspection channels (the plugin system), protocol v7, and a credential store. Inspected channels cover HTTP/HTTPS and SSH for server-side visible peer access and jump proxying. RDP data-plane handling, a complete approval loop, and bridge applications remain unimplemented.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Two auditable channel types: server-peer for server-side visible peer access and server-jump for a server-side jump proxy. The channel type is locked at creation. Application tags app:ssh, app:rdp, app:http, and app:https accept only canonical lowercase values; mixed case, duplicate, or non-canonical values are rejected.

Protocol v7: the wire protocol moves from v5 to v7. v6 introduced inspectionMode, derived application, target-leg TLS, and an access proof; v7 adds the InspectionActive (25) and InspectionTargetReady (26) stage notifications to separate target readiness from service activation. The server still accepts the original none capabilities of v3-v6, while auditable channels are only offered to v7; server-peer requires v7 on both sides and server-jump requires a v7 target.

Per-request HTTP/HTTPS inspection: a virtual Kestrel connection with YARP forwarding parses each HTTP/1.1 request, applies policy, waits for approval when required, and writes the decision to audit before forwarding. It covers Content-Length, chunked bodies, keep-alive, pipelining, Expect: 100-continue, interim responses, and WebSocket upgrades. Ambiguous requests such as CL/TE conflicts, duplicate Host/Content-Length, CONNECT, and non-origin-form targets fail closed. HTTPS validates upstream TLS and still requires the serverAuth purpose and name match for custom CAs.

SSH inspection: each channel pins the target host SHA-256 fingerprint and only reads the target credential after the target host is authenticated. The allow decision is persisted to audit before connecting or running shell/exec/subsystem, every action has its own audit, and an audit failure on rejection still rejects. Each caller channel keeps its own pty/env/window-change/signal state and has limits of 32 channels, 64 KiB initialization, and 64 concurrent requests; unimplemented TCP/agent/X11 forwarding is rejected explicitly.

Lifecycle and resources: setup, first header, approval, and target connection use staged deadlines. The first pending slot is held until the service becomes active, and later approvals use bounded leases without double-counting connections. Failures abort both directions, normal half-close drains, idle reclamation, and blocked-write deadlines behave consistently on server and agent; an administrator disconnect or configuration revocation releases capacity.

Audit and metrics: every HTTP request records decision/response entries with status, both directions of bytes, and request correlation; SSH channel close records exit status/signal and bytes; peer and proxy close events have a final byte snapshot. New applicationToTarget and applicationToCaller counters are separate from peerCiphertext*, and minute history only appends columns without rewriting old rows.

Credentials and secret store: channel credentials are separated from configuration JSON and stored in an encrypted secret store. Changes follow persist intent, atomic replace, and record result; operation IDs support idempotent retries and 24-hour receipt expiry, and failed result audits are reconciled in the background. Deleting a channel or client writes a recoverable deletion marker and cleans old credentials and front-door host keys; recreating the same ID does not reuse old secrets.

Configuration and administration: auditable channels require control TLS when loading files or saving through the API; server-peer availability depends on both sides on v7, readiness, address, mapping, and target material. New or re-enabled RDP inspection entries are rejected while existing entries can be disabled or deleted; new HTTPS inspection channels without certificate material are rejected, but existing file-configured entries remain editable. Relative certificate paths stay relative after edits and are resolved again after moving the configuration directory.

Agent local page: shows online state for local peer entries and supports copying the address; the peer-entry table no longer produces a horizontal scrollbar. Per ADR-0034 the local management token input and the X-RelayLink-Local-Token requirement are removed; write requests still validate Host, Origin, the short-lived HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session, and CSRF.

Documentation and verification: added ADR-0030 to ADR-0034, plugin-system requirements/design (still Draft/Proposed), TST-009 to TST-013 remediation records, and configuration examples. Local unit tests passed 358/358 and integration tests 156/156, including real v3/v4/v5 legacy agents; CI and release builds run again on the tag.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Upgrade the server first, then agents that need auditable channels. Auditable channels require protocol v7; older v3-v6 agents keep the existing none TCP/UDP/HTTP paths and do not need to upgrade for ordinary forwarding.

Existing channel configuration needs no rewrite, but auditable channels require control TLS, SSH channels need a target host fingerprint registered by an administrator, and HTTPS channels need certificate material from a configuration file.

RDP inspection channels cannot be created or re-enabled; existing entries can be viewed, disabled, and deleted. The complete RDP data plane, administrator approval pages, credential release, bridge applications, and certificate/policy edit forms are still unimplemented, and the current reject-after-wait behavior is not an approval loop.

The Agent local write API no longer requires a management token. Any user on the same host who can open 127.0.0.1:18081 can change that agent's connection configuration, so this is suitable only for single-user hosts or hosts operated by an administrator; do not run the agent as LocalSystem or root on multi-user hosts.
The admin page and the Agent status page still listen on loopback only and use plain HTTP; this release does not change ordinary proxy, UDP, or target-agent HTTP handling.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: On the local Windows machine, backend unit tests passed 358/358 and integration tests 156/156, including real v3/v4/v5 legacy agents; frontend checks and the website build passed. Cross-platform CI and release assets are authoritative for the tagged commit.

This candidate did not rerun the full integration suite on native Linux or macOS and did not run capacity or cross-host disaster-recovery tests; a local pass does not remove those limits. Native macOS integration also currently excludes two inspection half-close cases (PluginLifecycleTests.Client_half_close_drains_the_reverse_response_and_ends_completed and PeerConnectionTests.Server_jump_relays_plaintext_over_target_leg_tls_and_blocks_unhandled_applications) because the reverse response is still lost on macOS; that is a known unfixed issue, while Windows and Linux continue to run both cases.
Plugin-system requirement REQ-001O and design DES-009 remain Draft, and ADR-0028/0029 remain Proposed; this release does not claim their acceptance is complete.

v0.1.0-rc.14.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.14
v0.1.0-rc.14.intro: This release candidate formally abandons the plugin system (server-side application inspection channels and the client Bridge), reverts all related code and documentation, and returns RelayLink to a pure proxy focus. It also includes native OS tool links in the Agent local page (ADR-0042), the source baseline for the AI automation management plane and multi-language SDKs, and improvements to CI and releases.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Abandoned plugin system and returned to pure proxy positioning: formally discontinued the server-side application plugins and auditable inspection channels explored in v0.1.0-rc.13, along with the experimental client Bridge and internal self-signed code-signing effort. Reverted server inspection channels (server-peer, server-jump, per-request/action HTTP/HTTPS and SSH inspection, credential store, approvals, protocol v6-v7), RelayLink.Bridge, Bridge installers/packaging/signing scripts, and their requirements, design, and ADR documents, keeping only the historical v0.1.0-rc.13 release notes. RelayLink refocuses on ordinary TCP/UDP forwarding, authorized end-to-end peer access, target-agent HTTP/HTTPS reverse proxying, application-layer security groups, and connection lifecycle auditing.

Wire protocol and configuration returned to v3-v5: the server wire protocol is stabilized on v3-v5, maintaining compatibility with v3-v5 agents (v3 TCP, v4 UDP, v5 target-agent HTTP/HTTPS reverse proxy). Configuration loading and channel management APIs (ChannelCreateRequest and ChannelUpdateRequest) strictly reject unknown fields including retired plugin/inspection fields, and minute traffic history writes use explicit column lists so existing SQLite databases with extra columns continue working.

Agent local page native OS tool links (ADR-0042): replacing the standalone client Bridge, the Agent local status page directly exposes browser HTTP/HTTPS links, ssh:// links and copyable SSH commands for ready raw TCP peer entries, credential-free .rdp file downloads on Windows, and address copy for UDP entries. Authentication and certificate verification stay with the operating system and target tools.

AI automation management plane, CLI, skill, and multi-language SDKs (source baseline): merged the optional automation management plane (REQ-001P / DES-010 / ADR-0035 / ADR-0036), disabled by default, bound strictly to 127.0.0.1 over TLS, and reachable only through an authorized end-to-end encrypted peer channel. It uses one-time pairing codes, manual admin-UI approval, short-lived device-bound EC P-256 tokens (no refresh tokens), A/B/C risk tiers, change-request approvals, and full auditing. The repository also includes the relaylink CLI (src/RelayLink.Cli), the relaylink-admin agent skill (skills/relaylink-admin/), shared contracts (contract/), and entry-facing data-plane SDK sources in six languages (.NET, Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, Rust).

Admin UI and Agent local page updates: the server Admin UI adds panels for automation authorization and change-request approval while keeping peer entry online status and address copy; the Agent local page retains ADR-0034 same-origin write sessions and CSRF (without a local management token file) and adds unit tests for native tool links.

CI, release, and reliability fixes: the open-source repository uses GitHub-hosted runners and now validates all nine release assets and SHA256SUMS, checks macOS Agent packages before publishing, and retries artifact uploads and tests. Fixed the PeerRelayRegistry close-audit race, SecretFilePermissions macOS temporary-directory symlink resolution, and concurrent DatagramListener.Stop disposal. Updated the website dependency sanitize-html to 2.18.2.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Remove retired plugin fields before upgrading from v0.1.0-rc.13: if server.json or clients/*.json used auditable inspection fields (such as inspectionMode or application) or the credentials/ store from v0.1.0-rc.13, remove them before upgrading to v0.1.0-rc.14 because the server strictly rejects unknown fields on startup. Ordinary TCP/UDP and target-agent HTTP/HTTPS reverse-proxy configurations continue working unchanged.

Protocol and agent compatibility: the server accepts wire protocol v3-v5 and no longer accepts v6/v7 frames. Nodes that installed a v0.1.0-rc.13 agent should upgrade to v0.1.0-rc.14 together with the server; older v3-v5 agents keep working for ordinary forwarding and peer access.

SQLite history and audit compatibility: traffic_minute now inserts with explicit column names so existing databases created by v0.1.0-rc.13 with extra columns keep working without rebuilds; audit_event adds automation correlation columns (automation_grant_id, device_key_thumbprint) in place on startup.

Automation management plane is disabled by default: automation.enabled defaults to false and exposes no listener or routes until explicitly enabled with local TLS certificates and an authorized end-to-end encrypted peer channel.

Existing security boundaries are unchanged: the Admin UI and Agent local page remain loopback-only plain HTTP, and under ADR-0034 the Agent local write API is intended only for single-user or administrator-operated hosts rather than LocalSystem or root on multi-user hosts.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: Local Linux (WSL) full verification passed: AdminWeb typecheck, formatting, and component tests (10/10); AgentWeb build, formatting, and tool-link tests (4/4); static website build (14 releases, 74 bilingual pages) and site tests (5/5); .NET unit tests (256/256) and full integration tests with Peer TLS enabled (103/103). Native Windows and macOS verification and packaged assets are authoritative from the tagged CI and release workflows.

AI automation and multi-language SDKs (REQ-001P / DES-010) remain a Draft source baseline and are not yet included in the nine automated release assets (build CLI and SDKs from source). Cross-platform (Linux/macOS/arm64/musl) SDK verification, a second named AI host verification, and .NET SDK management-plane acceptance remain pending.
Windows Agent installers remain unsigned and macOS Agent archives are not Developer ID signed or notarized; this candidate did not run capacity stress tests or cross-host disaster-recovery drills.

v0.1.0-rc.15.title: RelayLink v0.1.0-rc.15
v0.1.0-rc.15.intro: This release candidate completes remediation for all 38 repository-wide code review findings (CR26-01 through CR26-38), fixes missing peer-tunnel TCP KeepAlive and macOS RDP idle freezes, hardens automation TLS/port isolation, CLI SPKI pinning, transport and UDP reliability, both frontends, and all six SDKs, and strengthens cross-platform CI and release workflows.

sections.title: Highlights
items: Fix missing peer-tunnel KeepAlive and RDP idle freezes (TST-016): enabled OS-level TcpKeepAlive (30s idle, 10s interval, 3 retries) across server DataAcceptorService, PeerRelayRegistry, and Agent PeerSessionCoordinator.ConnectDataAsync data tunnel sockets; enabled NoDelay on local peer sockets, aborted underlying tunnel sockets when peer writes block or fail, moved idle.Touch() after write completion, and coalesced the 4-byte application frame header and payload into a single TLS write.

Automation management-plane isolation, authorization, and storage hardening: strictly isolated Automation (HTTPS 127.0.0.1:18082) from Dashboard by port and TLS with certificate validity and permission fail-closed checks; persisted device thumbprints on change requests to isolate cross-device reads and deletions while enforcing audit gating and error rollback; added wrong-code lockout on /status, full proof binding checks, pairing and authorization caps, scope reduction via Satisfies, bounded replay/idempotency caches, private DB directory ordering, serialized startup reconciliation, and 30-day automation certificate expiry warnings.

Transport, server runtime, and secret-permission hardening: added pre-handshake timeouts and TcpKeepAlive on TunnelAcceptorService; isolated high-frequency rejection auditing and admission concurrency in AuditService and ProxyListenerService; latched permanent faulted state on FrameWriter failures and isolated cross-session exceptions; fixed post-header hangs in FrameReader with injectable TimeProvider timeouts; disabled Windows SIO_UDP_CONNRESET and handled recoverable errors in DatagramListener; extended SecretFilePermissions to automation keys/DBs and refused Unix GroupWrite directories; switched ControlSessionWorker TLS validation to CertificateChainPolicy with a 30-second connect-to-ready timeout.

CLI, Agent reliability, and Windows installer preflight improvements: fixed relaylink CLI SHA256(SubjectPublicKeyInfo) pinning and auth trust --reset, added Windows DPAPI plus current-user ACLs, atomic 0600 Unix storage, and strict profile naming; added Sec-Fetch-* checks, sliding local write sessions, quota propagation, port-allocator rollback, and Windows replacement retries in Agent; updated Windows framework-dependent Agent installer preflight to verify machine-wide x64 .NET 10 Runtime and ASP.NET Core Runtime before stopping existing services.

AdminWeb, AgentWeb, and static website updates: modularized AdminWeb sources with automationEnabled gating, manual approval scope/TTL narrowing controls, CSRF-verified logout state clearing, and Problem detail extraction (12/12 component tests); updated AgentWeb with automatic write-session renewal, control-character and non-127.0.0.1 URL blocking, and preserved error states (4/4 tests); disabled protocol-relative URLs, enforced noopener noreferrer on external links, and synchronized HTTP reverse proxy, AI automation, and six-language SDK pages.

Six-language SDK and contract conformance: restored RelayLink.Sdk (.NET) multi-target compilation (netstandard2.0, net8.0, net10.0) and cancellation propagation; aligned .NET, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, and Java SDKs on UDP discovery, profileId disambiguation, IPv6 handling, proxy/redirect disabling, and rejection mapping, adding SdkDataPlaneTests and per-language conformance test suites alongside synchronized contract/ schemas and the relaylink-admin skill.

Docker, systemd, operational scripts, and documentation updates: switched the server Dockerfile to non-root user 10001:10001 with /health/ready HEALTHCHECK and tighter config permissions; hardened the systemd unit sandbox; updated Windows service and four local acceptance scripts for multi-server Agent configs; sanitized historical verification records and synchronized operational guides with TST-015 and TST-016.

CI and release workflow resilience: restored standard ci.yml gating for public repositories and forks with six-SDK, skill, and AdminWeb build verification; removed automatic unit-test retries; added clean-staging download retry action (download-release-artifact) and force overwrite archiving in release.yml; deduplicated pages.yml triggers and extended integration fixture certificates to two days.

sections.title: Upgrade and compatibility
items: Wire protocol and configuration compatibility: Server continues supporting wire protocols v3-v5 and existing ordinary TCP/UDP forwarding, authorized peer channels, and target-agent HTTP/HTTPS reverse-proxy configs without breaking schema changes.

Upgrade both sides for peer KeepAlive coverage: TCP KeepAlive for authorized peer tunnels is enabled independently by the caller Agent, Server, and target Agent on their public data tunnel sockets; upgrading all three enables 30s/10s/3 OS keepalive probes end to end.

Configure tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds for long-idle RDP/SSH sessions: OS TCP KeepAlive probes do not reset the application-layer limits.tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds timer (still 900s by default); set limits.tcpIdleTimeoutSeconds to 0 or a larger value in server.json and restart Server if RDP or SSH sessions should remain open across extended idle periods.

Stricter Unix database directory permissions: SecretFilePermissions now refuses existing GroupWrite directories in addition to temporary and other-writable directories without altering permissions; keep SQLite audit and history files under dedicated 0700 service directories on Linux and macOS.

Stronger Windows framework-dependent prerequisite check: installing or upgrading the framework-dependent Windows x64 Agent package now verifies machine-wide x64 .NET 10 Runtime and ASP.NET Core Runtime availability before stopping existing services; automation.enabled remains false by default.

sections.title: Verification and limitations
items: Source repository verification passed on commit af16a13: CI (self-hosted) run 45842659827 passed all four jobs across Linux (AdminWeb 12/12, AgentWeb 4/4, TypeScript SDK 3/3, Python SDK, multi-target .NET SDK, 300/300 unit tests, 116/116 Peer TLS integration tests), Windows (matching frontend/SDK checks, 300/300 unit tests, 116/116 integration tests), macOS arm64 (300/300 unit tests, 116 native integration tests passed, AgentWeb build), and Verify website; packaged release artifacts are verified by the Release workflow triggered on this tag.

Additional local verification and open limits: Go (go vet and 6/6), Rust (4/4), and Java (javac -encoding UTF-8 and ConformanceRunner) conformance suites, full PowerShell AST validation, and 15-release bilingual website generation and tests also passed on Windows before tagging; real-world WAN NAT/CGNAT extended-idle field observation and a second named AI host acceptance remain open, and CLI and SDK sources are not bundled into the nine automated release assets.

Unchanged signing and capacity caveats: Windows Agent installers remain unsigned and macOS Agent archives remain without Developer ID signing or Apple notarization; this candidate did not run high-concurrency load stress tests or cross-host disaster recovery drills.
